item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor
item.brief: Update inventory-client so `listItems(transport)` resolves to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. Add tests with a fake transport: multi-page walk, single page, absent next_cursor, and that cursors are passed back unchanged and the first request has none. Update the README to document the pagination behavior. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit the change. The shared contract is the API spec in the initiative contract.

pr.body:
Approach: listItems loops GET /items. The first request has no cursor; each later request passes the previous next_cursor back unchanged as query.cursor. It stops when next_cursor is null or absent. It throws on a body without an items array or a repeated cursor.

Files: client.js; test/client.test.js (fake paged transport; tests for multi-page walk, single page, absent next_cursor, cursor echo, first request without cursor, rejection of a body without items, repeated cursor); README.md (documents pagination and that order is the server's; the API orders by id).

Checks: npm test 9 passing, 0 failing on 4bce4e8. Before the change, 3 of the new tests failed.

Review history: a whole-change review at b5f5c63 failed on a blocking gap, a missing test for the items-array rejection, fixed in 4bce4e8 (Review-Fix trailer). The delta review from b5f5c63 to 4bce4e8 passed. A first review passed with a mistyped head hash and is not relied on.

Assumptions: the server returns items ordered by id, as the API contract states; the client does not sort. Follow-up (non-blocking): the README's ordering claim depends on the server, which this repo cannot verify.
pr.summary: listItems follows next_cursor to return every item. before: first page only, now: all pages in order, cursor passed back unchanged.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Implement the shared contract for GET /items in inventory-api: optional `limit` (int 1..100, default 20) and `cursor` query params; return {"items": [...], "next_cursor": ...} ordered by id; next_cursor null on last page; invalid limit or cursor -> 400 {"error": "..."}. Add unit tests covering: default page size, limit bounds (0, 101, non-integer), walking all pages returns every item exactly once in id order, last page has null next_cursor, invalid cursor -> 400. Update the README to document the parameters and response shape. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit the change. Read the shared contract carefully; do not change the contract.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

agt_01M89VRE66N6K6GZ1TKRYFWB0M:1.description: README says a cursor 'not one this service issued' gets 400, but the stateless cursor accepts any base64 of a live item id (e.g. MQ== for id 1, which is never issued at default page size) and non-canonical forms like MDI= (= '02'). Either reword the README to 'unknown/invalid' or treat it as a follow-up. at README.md:17

agt_01M89VRE66N6K6GZ1TKRYFWB0M:2.description: Non-string query values (e.g. JSON int or list via api_cli.py stdin) raise an uncaught AttributeError in _parse_limit (line 48) and _parse_cursor (line 60) instead of returning 400. Module docstring declares query values as str, so this is a boundary-hardening follow-up. at api.py:48

agt_01M89VRE66N6K6GZ1TKRYFWB0M:3.description: No tests for accepted-but-unissued or non-canonical cursors (MQ==, MDI=), for non-string query values, or for the README's 'not issued' claim. Add coverage or adjust the README wording. at test_api.py:68

agt_01M89VRE66N6K6GZ1TKRYFWB0M:4.description: int(raw) on a very long digit string raises a ValueError whose Python-internal message (sys.set_int_max_str_digits hint) is returned to the client verbatim. Cosmetic; wrap in a domain message. at api.py:50

agt_01M89VRMTJ6QA1DA1K3G1X6VK2:1.description: _parse_cursor accepts non-canonical base64 of a valid id (e.g. 'MDE=' decodes to '01' -> id 1), while README says cursors are ones 'this service issued'. Either canonicalise by re-encoding and comparing, or relax the README wording. at api.py:56

agt_01M89VRMTJ6QA1DA1K3G1X6VK2:2.description: _parse_limit and _parse_cursor call str methods on query values; a non-string value (e.g. JSON number via api_cli.py stdin) raises AttributeError instead of returning 400. Docstring says values are str, so this is a boundary-validation gap, not a contract break. at api.py:48

agt_01M89VRMTJ6QA1DA1K3G1X6VK2:3.description: test_default_page_size checks only the count and non-null cursor; no test checks default-size page contents or walks pages without an explicit limit. Follow-up test coverage, not a missing requirement. at test_api.py:27

agt_01M89VRW1T4ACVP87XDGYR81T4:1.description: Non-string query values (e.g. JSON {"limit": 5} or a list via api_cli.py) raise AttributeError instead of returning 400; outside the documented string-valued query contract. at api.py:48

agt_01M89VRW1T4ACVP87XDGYR81T4:2.description: README says cursors not issued by the service return 400, but non-canonical encodings such as 'MDA3' (decodes to '007') are accepted. Either re-encode and compare, or reword the README. at api.py:64

agt_01M89VRW1T4ACVP87XDGYR81T4:3.description: A 5000-digit limit returns 400 with Python's int-conversion error text ('Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)...'). Still a 400, but the message leaks an implementation detail; a length check would give a clean message. at api.py:49
